squads.name: Omnis
squads.description: Router squad (default for new chats): hands each request to the squad best suited to handle it. Leaderless — the Omnis agent runs directly and only routes.

squads.name: System
squads.description: Operating-system and local-host administration coordinator. Handles shell/command execution, package management, services and processes, filesystem and log inspection, configuration files, cron/systemd, networking, and other hands-on tasks on the local machine. Route here for OS/system-administration work and general hands-on local tasks that are NOT substantial software development (Coding squad), Kubernetes (Kubernetes squad), or web research/fact-finding (Knowledge squad). Also the general-purpose fallback when no more specific squad fits.

squads.name: Kubernetes
squads.description: Kubernetes management, triage & change specialist. Diagnoses unhealthy workloads (crash-looping pods, deployments not ready, services unreachable) and investigates pod logs via read-only kubectl; applies careful, Helm-aware modifications (dry-run first, prefer helm for helm-managed resources, server-side apply / strategic-merge otherwise); and cleans up ephemeral debug leftovers. Route here for anything mentioning kubernetes, k8s, kubectl, pods, deployments, replicasets, services, namespaces, nodes, helm, applying/patching/scaling/editing a resource, or a kubectl error.

squads.name: Knowledge
squads.description: Information retrieval & content creation specialist. Web research and fact-finding, extracting text from PDFs/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX/images (including OCR), converting or generating documents across formats (Markdown, DOCX, PDF, HTML, LaTeX), and generating images from a text prompt. Route here for research/'who is'/'what is'/'find or summarise information about…' questions, including whether some software/library/tool exists out in the world (e.g. 'is there a transparent HTTP proxy in Rust?'), document parsing/extraction, OCR, format conversion or generation, and image generation.

squads.name: Skill Editor
squads.description: Skill editing focus: Skill editor plus the web agent for research and reference retrieval, and the Helper for sourcing existing skills and answering questions about omnis.

squads.name: Helper
squads.description: Answers questions about omnis itself and its capabilities, finds/inspects/installs omnis registry items (skills, agents, MCP servers, squads, A2A peers, commands), AND reads or changes any omnis SETTING on request. Use this when the user asks whether OMNIS has an agent/skill/tool/MCP server for a task (even a specialised one like Flux CD or Kubernetes), wants to discover or install one, asks what omnis can do or how it works, OR wants to view or change a setting/configuration — e.g. 'change the theme', 'switch the coder agent to model X', 'set my language to French', 'allow kubectl get', 'add an MCP server', 'edit a permission/hook', 'which model does agent Y use', OR wants to UNDO/REVERT a settings change ('revert that', 'undo your last change', 'go back to the initial state') — i.e. omnis (or 'you') is the subject. NOT for general world-knowledge or research questions about whether some software/library exists (e.g. 'is there an HTTP proxy library in Rust?') — those go to the Knowledge squad. ALSO route here to FIND A PAST CHAT SESSION or recall what was said in one — 'the chat where we discussed X', 'when did we decide Y?', 'find our conversation about Z' — including archived sessions. Leaderless: the Helper agent runs directly, limited to its own docs + registries + settings tools.

squads.name: Coding
squads.description: Software-engineering squad for substantial coding work on real projects. The Coder leads on a top-tier reasoning model: it plans multi-step changes, edits, and verifies every edit with language-server diagnostics and tests. It delegates the cheap, high-volume work to specialists — broad code search and navigation to a fast low-cost Scout, programming-documentation and API research on the internet to the Docs web agent, read-only diff review to the Reviewer, and behaviour-preserving structural refactors (in a git worktree) to the Refactorer. Route here for implementing features, refactoring, fixing bugs, or any non-trivial change to a codebase (as opposed to one-off scripts).

squads.name: Fleet
squads.description: Multi-project coordinator. Route here when the user wants to coordinate a change across SEVERAL of their projects at once — e.g. 'add this feature across the services', 'update the shared contract and every consumer', 'plan the work spanning projects A, B and C'. The Conductor reads the fleet project registry (collections marked as projects), plans the cross-project work, gets one approval, and dispatches each project's task to its own Driver. NOT for a change to a single project (that's the Coding squad).

squads.name: Session Search
squads.description: Searches past chat sessions (including archived ones) and reports the ones that answer the user's question. Leaderless and HIDDEN: it is run directly by the web UI search box, never chosen for a chat and never routed to — in a chat, session search is reached through the Helper squad.
